1: God has spoken through his Son
Long ago God spoke through the prophets; now he has spoken through his Son, who is the radiance of his glory and upholds all things. The Son is far above the angels, as many Old Testament texts show.
Jesus is God's final and complete word. He is not an angel or a prophet but the eternal Son.
2: We must pay close attention to what we have heard. Jesus, for a little while made lower than the angels, shared our flesh and blood, so that by dying he might destroy the power of death and help those who are tempted.
Because he suffered and was tempted, he can help us. He is not ashamed to call us brothers.
3: Moses was faithful as a servant in God's house; Christ is faithful as the Son over it. The Israelites who left Egypt hardened their hearts and did not enter God's rest. "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts."
Starting well is not enough. We need to encourage one another every day so that no one is hardened by sin.
4: A sabbath rest still awaits God's people, so let us strive to enter it. The word of God is living and sharper than any sword. We have a great high priest who sympathises with our weakness, so we can approach the throne of grace with confidence.
Jesus was tempted in every way as we are, yet without sin. We can come to him without fear.
5: A high priest called by God

Every high priest is chosen from among men and can deal gently with the weak. Christ did not take this honour for himself; God appointed him, a priest for ever in the order of Melchizedek. He learned obedience through what he suffered.
Christ's priesthood is the source of all priesthood. The author scolds readers who still need milk when they should be on solid food.
6: The author warns of the danger of falling away after receiving God's gifts, but is confident of better things for his readers. God's promise, backed by his oath, is a sure and steady anchor for the soul.
Hope is an anchor fixed where Jesus has already gone ahead of us.
7: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, blessed Abraham. Christ is a priest like him: not by descent from Levi, but by the power of an indestructible life. He lives for ever to intercede for us.
Jesus' priesthood never ends, so he can save completely those who come to God through him.
8: Our high priest serves in the true sanctuary in heaven. Jeremiah had foretold a new covenant, with God's law written on hearts and sins remembered no more. That covenant has come.
The Old Testament itself announced that something greater was coming.
9: The old tent had a Holy of Holies that the high priest entered once a year with the blood of animals. Christ entered heaven itself once for all with his own blood, winning eternal redemption.
The sacrifices of the Temple were shadows. Christ's one sacrifice is the reality, and the Mass makes it present.
10: The blood of bulls and goats could never take away sins. Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for ever. So let us draw near with confidence, hold fast to our hope, and not neglect to meet together.
Do not stay away from the assembly. Christian faith is lived with others, especially at worship.
11: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen. By faith Abel, Noah, Abraham, Sarah, Moses, Rahab and many others obeyed, endured and looked forward to a homeland they did not yet see.
The Old Testament saints lived by trusting God's promise. We are part of the same story.
12: Surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us run with perseverance, looking to Jesus. God disciplines us as a father disciplines his children. We have come to Mount Zion, the city of the living God.
Hardship can be the Father's training. Keeping our eyes on Jesus is how we finish.
13: Keep loving one another, welcome strangers, remember prisoners, honour marriage, and be content with what you have. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and for ever. Obey your leaders, and offer God a sacrifice of praise.
Faith shows in hospitality, purity and generosity. Christ does not change, whatever else does.
